questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of the first people to travel into space
How to use a map and compass when walking
How to find your way in space
Why GPS apps on phones are often wrong
questions.why: Rob says they'll hear that navigation at sea is easy compared to finding your way in outer space.

questions.q: What does Rob say about reading maps?
options: People use GPS and phone apps now
He is very good at reading all kinds of maps
He always carries a map when he travels
Maps are more accurate than mobile phones
questions.why: Rob says, 'this is the 21st century! Everyone uses GPS and mobile phone apps.'

questions.q: How did sailors find their way at sea in the past?
options: By following the coast and asking other ships
By using radio signals from the land
By watching the direction of the wind and waves
By using the stars and the Sun
questions.why: Sam says sailors used the stars and Sun to navigate.

questions.q: According to Ethan Siegal, why does a compass point north?
options: Because the Sun always rises in the north
Earth acts like it has a huge magnet inside
Because north is the highest point on Earth
Because the needle is pulled by the Moon
questions.why: He says Earth behaves like it has a giant bar magnet in it, and the needle points to the magnetic pole.

questions.q: What does Ethan say about calling north 'up'?
options: It's based on how the Earth moves in space
It was decided by early sailors for safety
There's no real reason for it
It's the only correct way to draw a map
questions.why: He says 'we've arbitrarily defined north' as up – decided by chance, not for a reason.

questions.q: Why does Sam mention Australia and South America being 'at the top'?
options: To show that maps in those countries are different
To explain why the southern hemisphere is colder
To say that most astronauts come from there
To show Earth can be seen either way up
questions.why: She says from space Earth can just as easily be seen the other way up, and 'both views are equally true'.

questions.q: Why is magnetism not a good guide in space, according to Ethan?
options: The magnetic field keeps changing direction
The black hole's magnetic field is too strong
Compasses stop working in zero gravity
Space has no magnetic fields at all
questions.why: He says the magnetic field 'flips irregularly' every few hundred or thousand light years.

questions.q: How do spacecraft find their way?
options: They follow signals sent from mission control
They sense the Sun's heat to find its position
They use very powerful magnetic compasses
They measure their distance from the Moon
questions.why: Sam says they use specialised heat sensors to detect the position of the Sun.
